tribe: Banu Asad ibn Khuzaymah (maternal lineage: Quraysh)
role: Occasion for revelation of verses on adoption (Quran 33:37)
summary: Zaynab bint Jahsh (RA) was a wife of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ whose marriage to the Prophet was directly commanded by Allah and recorded in the Quran (33:37). She was the cousin of the Prophet ﷺ through her mother Umayma bint Abd al-Muttalib, known throughout her life for extraordinary generosity to the poor, and was the first of the Mothers of the Believers to die after the Prophet ﷺ, passing away in 20 AH.
biography:
Zaynab bint Jahsh ibn Ri'ab al-Asadiyyah was born in Makkah around 590 CE. Her mother Umayma bint Abd al-Muttalib was an aunt of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, making Zaynab his cousin. She accepted Islam early among the Quraysh and was known for her beauty, noble lineage, and generosity of spirit.

The marriage that defined her historical significance was arranged by the Prophet ﷺ himself, who proposed that she marry his freed slave and adopted son Zayd ibn Harithah (RA). Zaynab and her brother initially resisted, considering the match beneath their social standing, but the Quranic revelation — 'It is not for a believing man or woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter, to have any choice in their affair' (Quran 33:36) — resolved their hesitation and the marriage proceeded. However, the marriage between Zaynab and Zayd was not harmonious. After Zayd sought permission from the Prophet ﷺ to divorce her and the Prophet initially counseled patience, revelation came decisively. When Zayd ultimately divorced her, Allah commanded the Prophet ﷺ to marry Zaynab himself, as recorded in Quran 33:37: 'And when Zayd had no longer any need for her, We married her to you, in order that there would not be any difficulty for the believers in regard to the wives of their adopted sons.' This marriage, contracted in approximately 5 AH, served a profound legislative purpose: it definitively established that adoption (tabanni) in the pre-Islamic sense — whereby an adopted son was treated as a biological son for all legal purposes — was not recognized in Islamic law. The Prophet ﷺ marrying his adopted son's former wife demonstrated this ruling in the clearest possible manner.

Zaynab herself was aware of this special significance. Ibn Sa'd records in al-Tabaqat al-Kubra (Vol. 8) that she would say with pride to the other Mothers of the Believers: 'Your families arranged your marriages, but my marriage was arranged by Allah from above the seven heavens.' This is referenced in the classical exegesis of al-Tabari and confirmed by al-Dhahabi in Siyar A'lam al-Nubala' (Vol. 2).

Beyond the Quranic distinction of her marriage, Zaynab was celebrated among all the companions for her extraordinary generosity to the poor. She was a skilled craftwoman — she tanned leather and sewed, then gave the proceeds entirely to those in need. Aisha (RA) is reported to have said about her: 'I have not seen a woman more complete in religion than Zaynab, more God-fearing, more truthful in speech, more connected to kin, more generous in charity, and more eager in doing everything that would bring her closer to Allah' (Ibn Sa'd, al-Tabaqat, Vol. 8; al-Dhahabi, Siyar, Vol. 2). Even Aisha, with whom Zaynab had the closest rivalries in terms of the Prophet's regard, acknowledged her virtues unreservedly.

She was also among the companions whose piety was tested during the incident of the ifk (the false accusation against Aisha) in 6 AH. When the Prophet ﷺ consulted Zaynab about Aisha's character, she testified to Aisha's virtue without any of the jealousy that the situation might have invited, saying that she knew only goodness of Aisha. Al-Bukhari records this testimony in Kitab al-Maghazi.

The Quran's command about the hijab for the Prophet's wives was connected to Zaynab's wedding feast, at which some guests lingered in the house beyond what was comfortable. The verses of hijab (Quran 33:53) were revealed on this occasion according to the account preserved by Anas ibn Malik (RA) in Sahih al-Bukhari (Kitab al-Nikah).

Zaynab (RA) died in 20 AH (641 CE) at the age of approximately 50, during the caliphate of Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA). Umar led her funeral prayer. She was the first of the Prophet's wives to follow him in death, and Umar arranged for her bier to be carried to the Baqi' cemetery. Al-Dhahabi describes her as one of the most distinguished of the Mothers of the Believers in worship, generosity, and the unique honour of having her marriage ordained by Quranic revelation.

key_events.event: Accepted Islam in Makkah; emigrated to Madinah
Married Zayd ibn Harithah (RA) at the Prophet's ﷺ arrangement
Divorced by Zayd; subsequently married to the Prophet ﷺ by divine command (Quran 33:37)
Occasion for revelation of hijab verses (Quran 33:53) during her wedding feast
Testified to Aisha's character during the incident of the ifk
Died in Madinah — first wife of the Prophet ﷺ to pass away after him; Umar led her prayer

notable_traits: Marriage ordained by Quranic revelation — unique among the Mothers of the Believers
Exceptional generosity — gave all proceeds of her craft work to the poor
Praised by Aisha (RA) despite their rivalry as the most complete in religion among the Mothers
Cousin of the Prophet ﷺ through her mother Umayma bint Abd al-Muttalib

key_relationships.mother: Umayma bint Abd al-Muttalib (aunt of the Prophet ﷺ)
key_relationships.first_husband: Zayd ibn Harithah (RA) — freed slave and former adopted son of the Prophet ﷺ
key_relationships.second_husband: Prophet Muhammad ﷺ (married ~5 AH by divine command)
key_relationships.brother: Abdullah ibn Jahsh (RA) — martyred at Uhud
